statements.status_notes: Allocation of resources without limits or throttling in the HTTP/2 HPACK decoder in Apache HttpComponents Core (5.4.2 and earlier, 5.5-beta1 and earlier) allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service through memory exhaustion by sending oversized compressed header blocks before the HTTP/2 SETTINGS acknowledgement causes the configured header list size limit to be applied.
statements.impact_statement: Apache HttpComponents Core HTTP/2 HPACK decoder memory exhaustion before the SETTINGS acknowledgement (GHSA-v3jc-474w-2wm6), fixed in httpcore5-h2 5.4.3 and 5.5-beta2. The scanned Liquibase Secure images carry httpcore5-h2 5.2.4 (Cassandra extension), and the Databricks extension carries a relocated copy below 5.4.3. The HPACK decoder only runs on HTTP/2 connections, and HttpComponents only negotiates HTTP/2 through its asynchronous client and server stacks (H2AsyncClientBuilder, HttpAsyncClients, H2 servers). Liquibase Secure code uses only the classic HTTP/1.1 client (the AWS SDK Apache client and the Ph-Eye filter). The Databricks JDBC driver bundled in the Databricks extension contains an HttpComponents async client that can negotiate HTTP/2, but the driver uses it only for its DBFS volume putFiles API and an unused incubator result fetcher; Liquibase calls neither, so no HTTP/2 connection is opened. The AWS extension excludes the AWS SDK's netty async client and builds its S3 client on the JDK URLConnection client. Liquibase Secure also runs no HTTP server.
